# s290 — Landing a schema bump runs the merge driver from the new code

`docs/landing.md` tells the person landing a slice that bumps the index or relay-roles schema to run the merge with the branch's slicer on PATH, and gives the one-line shim, so the merge driver can read both sides.

**Findings:** v1.11 relay 2026-10-15: landing s273 (index schema 8 to 9) on main; the `slicer-index` merge driver is `slicer merge-index` from PATH, which is the editable install of the main checkout and still at schema 8, so it refuses the schema-9 side (`schema_too_new` becomes an unreadable side and a text conflict on `.slicer/index.json`, confirmed by the s273 reviewer in a scratch merge); the orchestrator merged with a PATH shim running the branch's code · **Size:** S · **Tree:** docs

**Not in this slice:** changing the merge driver itself, and user projects, whose installed slicer is upgraded as a whole rather than per branch.

## Why

In this repo `slicer` on PATH is an editable install of the main checkout (AGENTS.md, Install). Git runs `slicer merge-index %O %A %B` from PATH during `git merge`, before main's `src/` has the branch's code. `mergeindex._load` refuses a side whose schema is newer than the code (`reject_future_schema`), so a schema-bump branch can never merge cleanly with the default driver. s273 hit this on 2026-10-15; s210 (schema 4 to 5) may have too.

## Files

- `docs/landing.md`: a short "Schema bumps" paragraph: how to tell (the slice's CHANGELOG or `SCHEMA_VERSION` in its diff), and the merge command with a PATH shim, for example `PATH=<dir with a slicer script running PYTHONPATH=.worktrees/<id>/src python3 -m slicer> git merge --no-ff ...`.
- `tests/test_docs_coverage.py` only if landing.md has a pinned shape.
